name: edges of a broken concrete pavement area laid on dirt: the cracked concrete pads break into the dirt in small irregular chunks with a subtle darker lip under the break, with outer and inner corners, the full interior filled with the cracked concrete slab field
label: wasteland_ruins/slab-edge

surfaces.part: cracked concrete pads and slab field on dirt, drawn as a flat ground plane seen from above

answer.evidence: This is a terrain autotile sheet: broken concrete patches on brown dirt, drawn flat from above. The silhouette is a full 256-wide field on every row. The column scans show repeating bands of dirt and concrete tones with no front-edge line, eave shadow or vertical face. The concrete chunks have only a thin darker lip at the breaks. There are no standing volumes, so there is no front face. For terrain this counts as a flat ground plane, not a standing 3/4-view object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate uses only about 12 colours in total. The concrete reads as roughly 3 grey steps (light, mid, a darker speckle) with no clear highlight or deep tone, against 5-7 steps on the paving reference. The dirt has speckle and grain, but it is a narrow brown ramp of about 3-4 tones. The measured 5 visible tones per tile is below the paving reference's 7 and above the grass's 3, and near-flat coverage is only 1%, so there are no large flat fills. Outlines are essentially absent. The concrete edge is a ragged value change with no darker lip under the break, which the brief asks for. The result looks like scattered grey blobs on dirt rather than a structured edge set. The 'full interior filled with cracked slab field' is just a flat grey rectangle with a few sparse crack lines. The outer and inner corner pieces are not clearly formed, and the pieces are laid out loosely and do not tile as a 4x3 patch. Shading is shallow, with no per-chunk highlight and no shadow lip, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar.

surfaces.part: cracked concrete pads (edge pieces and interior slab field)

answer.evidence: The sheet is a flat top-down terrain tileset: brown dirt fills the full 256px width, with irregular grey concrete patches (T, L and J shaped strips, a square pad, small chunks and a large cracked slab field at right with dark crack lines). The column scans show only alternating dirt tones and a concrete band, with no eave line, no front face and no vertical south face. The pieces are drawn as ground-level patches seen from above, so there is no standing volume, which fits terrain autotile content. The 'darker lip' under the breaks is only a thin 1-row shading, not a front face of 3+ rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a 4x3 layout, but it is not a clean autotile edge set. The concrete pieces are scattered, isolated blobs plus one rectangular slab, and the interior slab field is a small box rather than a full-tile fill. The concrete ramp is shallow: about 3 grey steps (light, mid, a speckle) against 5-7 tones in the paving reference. The dirt has some grain, about 3-4 browns, which is decent. The concrete chunks are stippled and speckled, so they are not flat fills. There is no outline. The break edges have only a faint darker lip and tiny dark flecks, which does not give the lip the brief asks for. The measured facts show 5 visible tones per tile, which is above the grass reference (3) and below the paving reference (7), with 1% flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edges. The measurements are acceptable, but the structure and shading depth are weaker than the references. Corners and edges are not clearly readable, and the concrete has no slab/crack structure outside the one box, so the full interior slab field is missing. A careful artist would not accept it next to the reference.
